board: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation (IDFPR)

cycle.label: Renewal period
cycle.note: Licensed CPAs renew every three years; the period runs October 1 – September 30. No carryover.

requirements.label: Personal development
requirements.note: Maximum, not a target. No more than 24 personal development hours count toward the 120.

requirements.label: Self-study
requirements.note: Maximum, not a target. No more than 80 hours of self-study (interactive and non-interactive combined) count per renewal period, and no more than 60 of them non-interactive (68 Ill. Adm. Code 1420.70). We use each course's delivery format — set it on each course.

requirements.label: Sexual harassment prevention
requirements.note: 1 hour each renewal (20 ILCS 2105/2105-15.5). It counts toward the 120. We count courses with "harassment" in the title — employer training only counts if the employer is an IDFPR-approved CE provider and issues a certificate.

newLicensee.note: Licensed CPAs are exempt from CPE for the first renewal after the license is issued.

licenseDateHint: Illinois licensed CPAs renew every three years on September 30.
issueDateHint: If your license was issued during this renewal period, no CPE is due for your first renewal.
limitsNotTracked: Non-interactive self-study: max 60 of the 80 self-study hours (certificates rarely say which).
recordRetention: Keep CPE records for at least 6 years.
toVerify: Personal development cap applied to the NASBA 'Personal Development' field only.
Both Regulatory and Behavioral Ethics count toward the 4 ethics hours (the rule says 'professional ethics').
First-renewal exemption: inferred when the issue date falls inside the current renewal period.
Registered (not licensed) CPAs have no CPE requirement — the app assumes a licensed CPA.
